about.title: Fair, traceable pathways from African farms to your table
about.lead: African Farmers Market connects East African farmers, artisans and artists with buyers around the world, so that every purchase visibly supports the people who grew or made it.
about.missionBody: Build ethical, transparent and traceable routes to market for African farmers: fair pay, care for the land, and impact that the community itself leads.
about.visionBody: Farmers valued as stewards of their land and culture, and trade that makes livelihoods and ecosystems stronger.
about.problemBody: Many rural farmers lack the tools to process and store what they grow, and are cut off from funding, certification, transport and buyers. Good harvests go unseen.
about.villageTitle: The Global Village Farm to Plate Project
about.villageBody: Our project to link African farmers directly with the people who eat their food. Ethical sourcing goes together with open storytelling, so you can see which families and villages your purchase supports.
about.traceBody: Scan the QR code on a jar or bag and you see where it came from, which villages harvested it and when. If a batch is ever recalled or put on hold, its passport says so first.
about.soulBody: Our name for the bond between the land, the people who work it, the things they make and you, the person who takes them home.
about.teamBody: A small team working across two continents: US operations in Colorado, and a farm in the Rungwe District of Tanzania.
about.eventsLead: Meet us in person, taste the honey and hear the stories.
about.eventsNoneWhy: New dates are shared in our newsletter first.
about.supplierTitle: Are you a farmer or maker in East Africa?
about.supplierBody: We are always looking for new partners.

stories.title: The people behind every jar, basket and painting
stories.lead: We buy directly from farmers, co-operatives and artists we know. These are a few of them.

illundo.name: The Illundo bee farmers
illundo.body: Beekeepers in the miombo woodlands harvest raw wildflower honey from their hives. We work with them directly, and the partnership opens new paid work for women in farming. Every jar of Mary's honey is traced to their harvest.

mary.name: Mary
mary.body: Mary is not one person. She stands for the many women farmers, teachers and entrepreneurs who hold their communities together. Our honey, our tea and our picture book carry her name.

benard.name: Benard Omondi, "Art Benny"
benard.body: Born and raised in Kibera, Benard studied fine art at Mwangaza Art School in Kisumu. He paints identity, resilience, daily life and mental health, and he illustrated The Mary.

nafasi.name: Nafasi Art Space
nafasi.body: A contemporary art centre with studios, galleries and workshops, open since 2008. Through Nafasi we show work by Pascal Masegesse, who paints memory and nature, and the surrealist portraits of Wilson Fantson Mpango.

rachel.name: Rachel Bosire
rachel.body: A maker who works with Kenyan women basket weavers. No two baskets are the same: the small differences are the mark of the hand that made them.

stories.artBody: Art that tells a bigger story. We show East African artists to make a connection, not only a sale.

faq.lead: Can't find your answer? Email us.

items.a: A bridge between African farmers, artisans and their communities and buyers around the world.
Our US operations are in Colorado. Our farm is in the Rungwe District of Tanzania.

items.q: Where do your products come from?
items.a: It depends on the product: each product page and batch passport shows its origin.
Most of it. A few items, such as shirts and stickers, are made to support the mission.
It builds direct, lasting routes to market, pays for tools and strengthens village economies.
Each batch has a QR code. Scan it to see where it came from, which villages harvested it and when, and whether it has been recalled or put on hold.
Usually 7 to 10 business days within the United States. Art and special items can take longer.
We don't take returns for a change of mind. If something arrives damaged, faulty or wrong, email us within 14 days with your order number and a photo.
For health reasons food can't be returned, unless it arrived spoiled or damaged. We can't refund for taste alone.

items.q: My basket looks different from the photo.
items.a: Every handmade piece varies a little. That is part of the craft, not a fault.
Yes, with Kenyan and Tanzanian artists, through our Art Nook.
